title: Wrecking Ball Demolition with Rigid Body Physics
prompt:
Create a single-HTML-file Three.js application simulating a wrecking ball on a chain demolishing a wall of stacked boxes with rigid body physics.

【Three.js Import (must follow exactly)】
Place in <head>:
<script type="importmap">
{ "imports": {
    "three": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/build/three.module.js",
    "three/addons/": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/examples/jsm/"
} }
</script>
Then in <script type="module">:
import * as THREE from 'three';
import { OrbitControls } from 'three/addons/controls/OrbitControls.js';

【Scene Setup】
- Background: dusty construction-site sky (#D4C5A9 to #87CEEB gradient)
- Camera: perspective, starting at (15, 10, 15) looking at (0, 3, 0)
- Lights: directional sun light (casts shadows), warm ambient, fill light from opposite side
- Ground plane: large flat plane, concrete-gray material, receives shadows
- OrbitControls with damping

【Crane Arm (static structure)】
- Vertical support pole: box (0.5 x 12 x 0.5) at position (-8, 6, 0), dark gray steel color
- Horizontal boom: box (16 x 0.4 x 0.4) at y=12, extending from x=-8 to x=+8
- The chain attaches at the boom tip (x=0, y=12, z=0) -- adjustable attachment point via slider

【Wrecking Ball and Chain (Verlet Integration)】
Chain modeled as a Verlet particle system:
- N=15 particles, connected by distance constraints
- Top particle pinned to the attachment point on the boom
- Each segment rest length = chainLength / N (chainLength adjustable, default 8m)
- Gravity: g = 9.81 m/s^2 on all particles
- Damping: velocity *= 0.999 per step (very light air resistance)
- Constraint iterations: 8 passes per frame for stability
- Integration: Verlet -- newPos = 2*pos - oldPos + acc*dt^2, dt=0.008s, multiple substeps per frame

Wrecking ball:
- Attached to the last particle of the chain
- Sphere geometry, radius 0.8m
- Dark heavy metal material (dark gray with slight specular)
- Mass: 50 kg (affects collision impulse calculations)

Chain visualization:
- Render as connected cylinder segments (small radius 0.05) between each pair of particles
- Or use THREE.Line with thick linewidth
- Metallic dark color

【Wall of Boxes (rigid body simulation)】
A wall made of stacked boxes:
- Grid: 5 columns x 6 rows = 30 boxes
- Each box: 1.0 x 1.0 x 1.0 unit cube
- Textured with crate.gif (loaded via TextureLoader)
- Wall positioned at x=5, centered at z=0
- Bottom row sits on the ground (y=0.5 for center)
- Small random offset (+-0.02) per box to prevent perfect stacking (more realistic)

Box rigid body physics (simplified):
Each box has:
- position: {x, y, z}
- velocity: {vx, vy, vz}
- rotation: Euler angles or quaternion
- angularVelocity: {wx, wy, wz}
- mass: 2.0 kg
- isStatic: false (becomes kinematic debris after settling)

Forces on each box:
- Gravity: -9.81 * mass in y
- Floor collision: if y < halfSize, push up and apply friction
- Box-box collision: AABB overlap test, push apart along minimum penetration axis, apply impulse
- Friction: mu=0.6 for box-floor, mu=0.4 for box-box
- Damping: velocity *= 0.98, angularVelocity *= 0.95 per step

【Ball-Box Collision】
When wrecking ball overlaps a box (sphere-AABB test):
- Calculate collision normal (from box center to ball center)
- Impulse: j = -(1 + e) * v_rel_dot_n / (1/m_ball + 1/m_box)
- Restitution e = 0.3
- Apply impulse to box: box.velocity += (j / m_box) * normal
- Apply angular impulse: box.angularVelocity += cross(contactPoint - boxCenter, impulse) / I_box
- The ball's chain particles also receive reaction force (slowing the ball)
- Boxes hit by ball should scatter realistically: fly outward, tumble, land and slide

【Swing Mechanics】
The wrecking ball swings as a pendulum:
- Press 'Space' to "pull back" the ball: move it to a raised position (x = attachment_x - chainLength*0.7, y = attachment_y - chainLength*0.3)
- Release 'Space' to let it swing (just release the hold, gravity does the rest via Verlet)
- The ball swings toward the wall, hits boxes, transfers momentum
- After impact, ball swings back (reduced energy), can swing again
- Press 'Space' again to pull back for another swing

【Controls】
(1) Chain length slider (id='slider-chain'): range 4 to 10, step 0.5, default 8
(2) Attachment point slider (id='slider-attach'): range -4 to 4, step 0.5, default 0 (x-position along boom where chain attaches)
(3) Ball mass slider (id='slider-mass'): range 20 to 100, step 5, default 50
(4) Keyboard: 'Space' hold to pull back ball, release to swing. 'R' to rebuild wall (reset all boxes). 'N' to reset everything (wall + ball at rest).

【HUD (id='hud')】
Semi-transparent panel at top-left:
- id='hud-boxes-standing': Number of boxes still in the wall (approximately upright and stacked)
- id='hud-boxes-fallen': Number of boxes displaced from original position
- id='hud-ball-speed': Wrecking ball speed in m/s (1 decimal)
- id='hud-ball-height': Wrecking ball y-position (1 decimal)
- id='hud-swings': Number of swings performed
- id='hud-chain-length': Current chain length (1 decimal)

【State Management】
Update window.__3D_STATE__ every frame:
{
  frameCount: number,
  boxesStanding: number,        // boxes still approximately in wall formation
  boxesFallen: number,          // boxes knocked out of formation
  totalBoxes: number,           // always 30
  ballPos: {x, y, z},          // wrecking ball world position
  ballSpeed: number,            // ball scalar speed (m/s)
  ballMass: number,             // current mass setting
  chainLength: number,          // current chain length
  attachX: number,              // attachment x-position on boom
  swingCount: number,           // number of swings performed
  isPulledBack: boolean,        // true while Space is held
  particleCount: number,        // number of chain particles
  isPaused: boolean,
  simTime: number
}

Box classification:
- A box is 'standing' if it is within 0.5 units of its original x/z position AND its y-position is within 0.5 of its original y AND its tilt from upright is < 30 degrees
- Otherwise it is 'fallen'

【Physics Constraints】
- Wrecking ball pendulum period should approximate T = 2*pi*sqrt(L/g) for small swings
- Ball impact should transfer momentum proportional to ball mass and speed
- Boxes should scatter outward from impact point, not all in the same direction
- Stacked boxes above a knocked-out box should fall due to gravity (no floating)
- After wall is fully demolished, all boxes should come to rest on the ground
- Chain segments must maintain length constraints (within 5% of target per segment)

Output a single HTML file.
physics_constraints: Verlet chain with 15 particles, 8 constraint iterations per frame, dt=0.008s. Impulse-based ball-box collision (e=0.3). AABB box-box collision with push-apart. Box rigid body: gravity, floor collision, friction (mu=0.6 floor, 0.4 box-box). Damping 0.98 linear, 0.95 angular. Ball pendulum period ~ 2*pi*sqrt(L/g). 30 boxes in 5x6 grid, mass 2kg each. Ball mass 50kg default.
difficulty_analysis: L5: (1) Verlet chain with constraint solving for the crane chain; (2) Sphere-AABB collision detection and impulse response for ball-box; (3) Box-box AABB collision with minimum penetration axis resolution; (4) Angular impulse and tumbling dynamics for boxes; (5) 30 rigid bodies with O(n^2) pair collision; (6) Pull-back and release swing mechanic via Verlet; (7) Box standing/fallen classification; (8) Chain reaction -- removing support causes upper boxes to fall; (9) Combined Verlet (chain) and Euler (boxes) simulation.
